title: Ansel and the Hollow Revisited
premise: Xanthe Villalobos, a memory-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers tonight's date inscribed in a century-old prophecy ledger — and realizes the guild has been quietly feeding the Hollow Gate the memories it needs to stay shut. When Xanthe learns the gate feeds on forgotten truths rather than mere memories, they must choose between exposing the guild's founding lie (which could reopen an ancient war) or letting their own name be erased to seal it forever. In the end, Xanthe sacrifices their recorded identity to the gate, but smuggles the truth into a new blank ledger, trusting a loyal friend to remember what the world will forget.
about_author: Quentin Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging sealed collections in private libraries before turning to fiction. They write about ledgers, gates, and the people history chooses not to remember.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A quiet night of inventory in the guild's vaults establishes Xanthe's invisible life among impossible objects. They find tonight's date written in a prophecy book dated a hundred years past. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Xanthe tests the prophecy entry against guild records and finds matching dates for other nights — all entries that were later redacted by someone with keeper's authority. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the thrill and dread of discovery.

chapters.title: The Guild of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Xanthe navigates the guildhall's politics, observing Master Corvane and the traders who broker forbidden bargains. We learn keepers are chosen for having no family to miss them. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as belonging.

chapters.title: What the Gate Eats
chapters.summary: Xanthe visits the Hollow Gate on maintenance rounds and notices fresh erosion where old memories should hold it shut. The gate whispers a fragment of Xanthe's own childhood back at them. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: violation.

chapters.title: A Friend Named Wren
chapters.summary: Wren, a guild courier with a talent for being unremarkable, helps Xanthe trace the redactions. Their easy banter reveals Wren knows more about the gate than she admits. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: warmth and first suspicion.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Master Corvane summons Xanthe, praising their discretion while probing how much they've read. He gifts them a rare memory-vial — a bribe or a warning. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: flattered, then chilled.

chapters.title: The Century Gap
chapters.summary: In the deep archive, Xanthe finds a hundred-year span of ledgers burned or missing, ending the night the last war ended. The prophecy book was written by the first keeper. POV: alternating Xanthe and Wren. Emotional beat: vertigo of scale.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren admits she was sent to watch Xanthe years ago but chose loyalty over orders. She reveals the guild doesn't guard the gate — it feeds it, one erased person at a time. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: guilt turned to alliance.

chapters.title: Names in the Margin
chapters.summary: Xanthe deciphers marginalia showing every erased keeper's name hidden in the prophecy text — including, on the final page, their own. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: terror becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Traders' Bargain
chapters.summary: A faction of traders, led by the elegant Madame Ossory, offers Xanthe protection in exchange for the prophecy book — they want the gate opened and the old powers restored. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Memory of a Door
chapters.summary: Xanthe enters the gate's threshold-dream and witnesses the ancient war's true origin: the 'impossible things' were people, transformed and traded. The gate is their collective grief. POV: dream sequence, Xanthe. Emotional beat: horror and pity.

chapters.title: Redaction
chapters.summary: Corvane discovers Xanthe's investigation and erases a week of their memories as punishment — but Xanthe left themselves notes. Relearning their own conclusions, they understand exactly what erasure costs. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: grief for a self half-lost.

chapters.title: The Blank Ledger
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Wren steal a blank keeper's ledger from the vault — the only object that can record truth the gate cannot digest. Ossory's traders shadow them through the stacks. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: desperate camaraderie.

chapters.title: Ossory's Truth
chapters.summary: Ossory corners Xanthe and argues her case: the gate imprisons innocents, and opening it is mercy. Her sincerity unsettles Xanthe more than any threat. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: doubt sharpened into moral complexity.

chapters.title: Corvane Unmasked
chapters.summary: Xanthe confronts Corvane with the redactions; he confesses he was the first keeper's apprentice, kept alive by the gate itself, trading centuries of names for a stalemate he no longer believes in. POV: Corvane. Emotional beat: weary villainy revealed as cowardice.

chapters.title: The Prophecy Fulfilled
chapters.summary: The date arrives. The gate stirs; across the city, forgotten things surface — lost voices, returned ghosts. The guild fractures as traders side openly with Ossory. POV: multiple, brief vignettes. Emotional beat: dread made citywide.

chapters.title: Siege of the Vault
chapters.summary: Ossory's faction storms the guildhall for the blank ledger. Wren holds the stair alone so Xanthe can reach the gate; Corvane, choosing his final side, buys them time with his own memories. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: sacrifice without ceremony.

chapters.title: The Choice of Keepers
chapters.summary: At the gate, Xanthe faces the choice the prophecy demands: feed it a name willingly given, or let it break. They realize willing sacrifice — not stolen memory — can seal it permanently. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: clarity after fear.

chapters.title: Xanthe Villalobos, Erased
chapters.summary: Xanthe gives the gate their name and every memory anyone holds of them, writing the whole truth into the blank ledger first. The gate seals; Ossory's power collapses mid-claim. POV: Xanthe, dissolving. Emotional beat: sorrow transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Remembered
chapters.summary: Wren wakes in a world where no one knows Xanthe existed — except her, because she read the ledger before its ink went silent. She carries the secret alone. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief braided with resolve.

chapters.title: A New Keeper
chapters.summary: The guild, rebuilt under reluctant reform, needs a keeper for the sealed gate. Wren volunteers, hiding the ledger in plain sight among the shelves. Corvane, memoryless, trains her without knowing why she smiles at him. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: bittersweet continuity.

chapters.title: Ansel and the Hollow, Revisited
chapters.summary: Years later, Wren teaches a young apprentice the ledger tradition and reads aloud a name no record contains: Xanthe Villalobos. Somewhere behind the gate, something listens — and remembers being remembered. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet hope; memory outlasting erasure.
